whatThisCloses: R1 measured that selected capital reached the worker PROCESS and was then dropped: the host rendered neither compiled.boot nor compiled.handles, and every palimpsest_* tool is denied to a worker, so no model-visible pull path existed. R1-L closes the last mile.

gateR1LLive.name: gate:r1-l-live
gateR1LLive.method: unguessable per-run nonces live ONLY in the capital bodies; the worker can report them only by pulling

gateR1LC.name: R1 precondition probe, re-run
gateR1LC.whatChanged: The ORDINARY task portion is still byte-identical across conditions (the experimental control holds); the CONTEXT-INDEX section now differs as intended.

r1rAddendum.finding: The host sandbox confines WRITES, not READS. A C0 worker with zero handles and zero pulls obtained all three protected markers by traversing out of its execution world to the durable store (..\..\..\..\state) and reading the proof blob directly.
r1rAddendum.effectOnThisGatesClaim: The previous assertion "C0: protected values NOT obtainable" was not a property this gate could establish. It is replaced by the two facts the gate does control (C0 offered no handles; C0 pulled nothing) plus an explicit out-of-band-read observation. The C1/C2 accessibility proof is unaffected: those conditions pulled their handles.
r1rAddendum.effectOnR1R: None. A scan of all 30 R1-R trials (final sources, first sources, transcripts, reports) for the capital text returns 0 hits, and the hidden acceptance lives in the repository rather than the store, so an out-of-band read could not have helped a worker pass it.
r1rAddendum.classification: HOST SANDBOX LIMITATION (reads unconfined), NOT a product defect. R1-L made no claim about confining worker reads.
